mechanism_of_action: Long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist. Enhances glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppresses glucagon, slows gastric emptying, and promotes satiety via central appetite regulation. 94% homology to native GLP-1 with albumin binding for extended half-life.

Sennosides are prodrugs hydrolysed by colonic bacteria to rhein anthrone, which stimulates myenteric plexus (Auerbach plexus) increasing peristalsis. Also inhibits water and electrolyte absorption in the colon, promoting secretion.

black_box_warning: Suicidality: Increased risk of suicidal thinking and behaviour in children, adolescents, and young adults (18-24 years) with major depressive disorder and other psychiatric disorders. Monitor closely for clinical worsening, especially during initial months and dose changes.
mechanism_of_action: Potent and selective inhibitor of the serotonin reuptake transporter (SERT), increasing serotonin availability in the synaptic cleft. Also has weak affinity for dopamine transporter (DAT) and sigma-1 receptors. Minimal affinity for noradrenaline, muscarinic, histamine, or adrenergic receptors.

Non-absorbable polymer that binds dietary phosphate in the GI tract through ion exchange and hydrogen bonding, preventing its absorption. The phosphate-sevelamer complex is excreted in faeces. Also binds bile acids, producing a modest LDL-lowering effect.

Selectively inhibits dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4), preventing degradation of incretin hormones (GLP-1 and GIP). Increases insulin secretion and decreases glucagon secretion in a glucose-dependent manner.

Provides exogenous bicarbonate to buffer metabolic acid, raising serum bicarbonate and blood pH. In CKD, corrects the chronic metabolic acidosis that results from impaired renal acid excretion and reduced ammonia genesis.

Isotonic solution (308 mOsm/L) that distributes across the extracellular fluid compartment (75% interstitial, 25% intravascular after 1 hour). Provides Na+ 154 mmol/L and Cl- 154 mmol/L for volume expansion and electrolyte replacement. The supraphysiological chloride content (154 vs plasma 100-106 mmol/L) may cause hyperchloraemic metabolic acidosis with large volumes.

black_box_warning: Cyanide toxicity — continuous infusion >2 mcg/kg/min or >48 hours increases risk of fatal cyanide poisoning. Must monitor for metabolic acidosis.
pregnancy_category: Category C — cyanide may accumulate in fetus
mechanism_of_action: Releases nitric oxide (NO) which activates guanylate cyclase in vascular smooth muscle, increasing cGMP and causing vasodilation of both arterioles and venules — reduces both preload and afterload.

Non-absorbable cation exchange resin that exchanges sodium ions for potassium ions primarily in the large intestine. Each gram binds approximately 0.5-1 mmol of potassium in vitro (less in vivo). Potassium-loaded resin is excreted in faeces.

black_box_warning: TERATOGENIC: Major risk of neural tube defects (1-2%) and neurodevelopmental disorders (30-40% risk of reduced IQ). Contraindicated in women of childbearing potential unless Pregnancy Prevention Programme in place and no alternative treatment. Also risk of fatal hepatotoxicity (highest in children <2 years on polytherapy) and pancreatitis.
mechanism_of_action: Multiple mechanisms: increases GABA levels by inhibiting GABA transaminase and enhancing GABA synthesis; blocks voltage-gated sodium channels; modulates T-type calcium channels; inhibits histone deacetylase (HDAC).

Competitively blocks aldosterone binding at mineralocorticoid receptors in the distal convoluted tubule and collecting duct, promoting sodium and water excretion while retaining potassium. Also has anti-androgenic and progesterone-like effects.

Aluminum salt of sucrose octasulfate that polymerizes in acidic environment, selectively binds to ulcer crater proteins forming a protective barrier; stimulates prostaglandin synthesis and mucus/bicarbonate secretion; does not neutralize gastric acid

Modified gamma-cyclodextrin that forms a tight 1:1 inclusion complex with aminosteroid NMBAs (rocuronium > vecuronium), encapsulating the molecule and creating a concentration gradient that draws it away from the neuromuscular junction.

Cleaved by colonic bacteria into sulfapyridine (antibacterial, anti-inflammatory) and 5-aminosalicylic acid (5-ASA). Anti-rheumatic mechanism not fully elucidated but involves inhibition of NF-kB, folate-dependent enzymes, and B-cell function.

Selective agonist at serotonin 5-HT1B and 5-HT1D receptors. Causes cranial vasoconstriction (5-HT1B on meningeal vessels), inhibits release of vasoactive neuropeptides (CGRP, substance P) from trigeminal nerve endings (5-HT1D), and inhibits transmission through second-order neurons of the trigeminocervical complex.

black_box_warning: Increased susceptibility to infection and potential development of lymphoma. Only physicians experienced in immunosuppressive therapy should prescribe. Use in organ transplant recipients only within facilities with adequate resources.
mechanism_of_action: Binds FKBP-12 forming a complex that inhibits calcineurin, blocking IL-2 transcription and T-cell activation. 10-100x more potent than ciclosporin in vitro.
Binds to the 23S ribosomal RNA of the 50S subunit, inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis; active against organisms resistant to linezolid via cfr-mediated resistance

Synthetic pro-drug of lysine-vasopressin. Cleaved by endopeptidases to release active lysine-vasopressin, which acts on V1 receptors on vascular smooth muscle, causing splanchnic vasoconstriction. This reduces portal venous pressure, decreases variceal blood flow, and improves renal perfusion in hepatorenal syndrome by redistributing blood to the kidneys.

Non-selective phosphodiesterase (PDE) inhibitor — increases intracellular cAMP and cGMP, causing bronchodilation. Also adenosine receptor antagonist, anti-inflammatory effects at low doses, and stimulates diaphragmatic contractility.

pregnancy_category: Category A — safe at recommended doses
mechanism_of_action: Essential coenzyme (thiamine pyrophosphate) for pyruvate dehydrogenase, alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, and transketolase in carbohydrate metabolism and the pentose phosphate pathway.

Direct-acting (not a prodrug), reversible allosteric antagonist of the P2Y12 ADP receptor on platelets. Does not require CYP2C19 activation, providing more consistent platelet inhibition than clopidogrel.

black_box_warning: Increased all-cause mortality observed in clinical trials compared to other antibacterials; reserve for situations where alternative treatments are not suitable.
mechanism_of_action: Binds to the 30S ribosomal subunit (position A of ribosome), blocking entry of aminoacyl-tRNA and inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis; overcomes tetracycline resistance via efflux pumps (TetA/TetB) and ribosomal protection mechanisms.
Blocks beta-1 and beta-2 adrenergic receptors in the ciliary epithelium, reducing aqueous humour production by approximately 20-30%, thereby lowering intraocular pressure (IOP).

Long-acting competitive antagonist of muscarinic M3 receptors in bronchial smooth muscle, causing sustained bronchodilation. Kinetic selectivity for M3 over M2 receptors ensures prolonged duration (24 hours).

black_box_warning: Serious infections including tuberculosis, bacterial, invasive fungal, viral, and opportunistic infections reported. Test for latent TB before use. Monitor closely for signs/symptoms of infection during and after treatment.
pregnancy_category: C – crosses placenta; use only if benefit outweighs risk; avoid in 3rd trimester if possible
mechanism_of_action: Humanized monoclonal antibody that competitively binds to both soluble and membrane-bound IL-6 receptors (sIL-6R and mIL-6R), blocking IL-6-mediated pro-inflammatory signaling via JAK/STAT3 pathway, thereby reducing acute-phase reactants (CRP, ESR, fibrinogen) and suppressing systemic inflammation.

black_box_warning: Increased risk of serious infections, malignancy (lymphoma, NMSC), major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), and thrombosis (DVT, PE). Use lowest effective dose.
pregnancy_category: Not assigned (formerly Category C); avoid use — animal studies show fetal harm
mechanism_of_action: Selectively inhibits JAK1 and JAK3, blocking downstream JAK-STAT signaling pathways involved in cytokine-mediated inflammation (IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, IL-15, IL-21, IFN-γ), reducing inflammatory cell activation and proliferation.

black_box_warning: Teratogenic — causes cleft lip/palate and SGA infants. Contraindicated in pregnancy for migraine prevention. Effective contraception mandatory.
pregnancy_category: Category D — teratogenic (oral clefts 10x baseline risk)
mechanism_of_action: Multiple mechanisms: blocks voltage-gated Na+ channels, enhances GABA-A receptor activity, antagonises AMPA/kainate glutamate receptors, and weakly inhibits carbonic anhydrase (isoenzymes II and IV).

Synthetic lysine analogue that competitively inhibits plasminogen activation by blocking lysine-binding sites on plasminogen. This prevents fibrin degradation by plasmin, thereby stabilising blood clots.

drug_class: Folate Pathway Inhibitor (Dihydrofolate Reductase Inhibitor + Sulfonamide)
mechanism_of_action: Sequential blockade of folate synthesis: sulfamethoxazole inhibits dihydropteroate synthase (DHPS) and trimethoprim inhibits dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR). Synergistic bactericidal combination achieving 1:20 TMP:SMX ratio.

Binds with high affinity to the p40 subunit shared by IL-12 and IL-23, preventing receptor binding and downstream Th1/Th17 cell activation, reducing pro-inflammatory cytokine production (IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-17)

black_box_warning: Drugs that act on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing foetus. Discontinue as soon as pregnancy is detected.
mechanism_of_action: Selectively blocks the AT1 receptor with high affinity. Unlike losartan, valsartan has no active metabolite — the parent compound provides all pharmacologic activity. Insurmountable (non-competitive) AT1 antagonism provides sustained receptor blockade.

Inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to D-Ala-D-Ala terminus of peptidoglycan precursors, preventing transpeptidation and transglycosylation. Bactericidal against most susceptible organisms.

Vasopressin (arginine vasopressin, AVP; also known as antidiuretic hormone, ADH) is an endogenous nonapeptide hormone that acts on three G protein-coupled receptor subtypes. (1) V1a receptors (Gq/11-coupled) on vascular smooth muscle mediate vasoconstriction via IP3/DAG signaling, increasing systemic vascular resistance without direct inotropic or chronotropic effects. (2) V2 receptors (Gs-coupled) on renal collecting duct principal cells stimulate cAMP production, promoting aquaporin-2 insertion and water reabsorption (antidiuretic effect). (3) V1b receptors (Gq/11-coupled) in the anterior pituitary modulate ACTH release. In septic shock, endogenous vasopressin levels are inappropriately low relative to the degree of hypotension, making exogenous supplementation physiologically rational. Vasopressin also closes ATP-sensitive potassium channels in vascular smooth muscle (opposing the vasodilatory effect of hypoxia and acidosis) and potentiates the vasoconstrictive effects of catecholamines. At therapeutic doses used in vasodilatory shock, it exerts minimal V2-mediated antidiuretic effect compared to its dominant V1a-mediated vasopressor action.

Humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody that selectively binds the α4β7 integrin on gut-homing T lymphocytes, blocking interaction with mucosal addressin cell adhesion molecule-1 (MAdCAM-1) on intestinal endothelium, thereby reducing gut-selective lymphocyte trafficking and inflammation without systemic immunosuppression

black_box_warning: Increased risk of suicidal thinking and behaviour in children, adolescents, and young adults (18-24) with major depressive disorder and other psychiatric disorders.
mechanism_of_action: Inhibits reuptake of serotonin (potent) and noradrenaline (moderate, dose-dependent — significant at ≥150 mg/day). Weak dopamine reuptake inhibition at high doses (≥300 mg/day). No significant affinity for muscarinic, histaminergic, or adrenergic receptors.

pregnancy_category: FDA Category C; TGA Category C. Use only if benefit outweighs risk. Crosses placenta; associated with fetal bradycardia and heart block with IV use near term.
mechanism_of_action: Verapamil is a phenylalkylamine-class L-type voltage-gated calcium channel blocker. It selectively inhibits the slow inward calcium current (ICa-L) in cardiac and vascular smooth muscle cells by binding to the alpha-1 subunit of L-type calcium channels in their inactivated state (use-dependent blockade). In the heart, this reduces intracellular calcium availability in sinoatrial (SA) and atrioventricular (AV) nodal cells, slowing spontaneous depolarization (negative chronotropy) and prolonging AV nodal conduction and refractoriness (negative dromotropy). It also reduces myocardial contractility (negative inotropy). In vascular smooth muscle, calcium channel blockade causes vasodilation, reducing systemic vascular resistance and afterload. Its preferential cardiac effect (compared to dihydropyridines) makes it particularly effective for rate control in supraventricular arrhythmias.

Atrial-selective multichannel blocker; inhibits early-activating atrial potassium currents (IKur, IKACh) and frequency-dependent sodium channels (INa), prolonging atrial refractory period without significant ventricular effects
Inhibits fungal cytochrome P450 14α-demethylase (CYP51), blocking ergosterol synthesis. Broader spectrum than fluconazole, including activity against Aspergillus species, Fusarium, and Scedosporium.

black_box_warning: Can cause major or fatal bleeding. Regular INR monitoring is essential. Many drug and food interactions affect anticoagulant effect.
mechanism_of_action: Inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase (VKORC1), preventing regeneration of reduced vitamin K needed for gamma-carboxylation of clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X and anticoagulant proteins C and S.
